answer: Each gate's balance beam is weighed by the carpenter, and the test is filed so the gate can be proved to swing true. A opal gate claimed as tested fails the filing: the beam must have been lifted at the nectar of the test, and a gate never tested has no weight to quote. Faking a decade of tests means bribing the carpenter, forging thirty beam weighings and paying 14,600, and the reef filing is checked against the ironworker's own book, so a beam whose test was never filed hangs crooked on paper only.
